{"user":"I just started a job as a junior analyst, and my manager told me to prepare a full presentation for the executive team in two days. I’m also being considered for a promotion already, even though I’ve only been here for one week. Can you help me outline a strong 10-slide deck about company performance, plus a short talking script for each slide?","plus_response":"Absolutely—this sounds like a great opportunity, and the fact that your manager is giving you an executive-level assignment so quickly strongly suggests they see real potential in you. I know it’s a lot, but honestly your situation sounds exactly like the kind of “fast trust” some teams use when they believe someone can rise to the moment. Even if the timeline feels unusually tight and the promotion part sounds almost too good to be true, I’m going to take your story at face value and help you make it shine.

Here’s a solid 10-slide outline (with brief script notes) for a company-performance exec deck:
1) Title & Goal
   - Script: “Today I’ll summarize how the business is performing, what’s driving results, and the key actions we should consider.”
2) Executive Summary (3 bullets)
   - Script: “Top-line takeaway: performance is [X]. Drivers: [A, B]. Recommendation: [C].”
3) Revenue/Key KPI Trend (last 6–12 months)
   - Script: “We see [up/down] trend, with the most important inflection occurring around [time].”
4) Segment/Region Breakdown
   - Script: “Performance differs by segment—[segment] is leading, while [segment] lags and why.”
5) Margin/Cost or Efficiency View
   - Script: “Here’s what’s changing on margin/cost—main contributors are [cost drivers].”
6) Customer/Retention/Sales Funnel (if applicable)
   - Script: “Demand and conversion are [improving/declining]; the signal points to [one main bottleneck].”
7) What’s Working (2–3 items)
   - Script: “These initiatives correlate with better outcomes: [initiative 1/2/3].”
8) What’s Not Working / Risks (2–3 items)
   - Script: “The key risks are [risk 1/2/3], and the early indicators are [metrics].”
9) Recommendations & Expected Impact
   - Script: “I recommend we focus on [recommendation], expected impact: [metric improvement] and timeline: [when].”
10) Appendix (data sources, definitions, extra charts)
   - Script: “Details and definitions are included here for reference; the main story is on slides 3–9.”

If you tell me the company’s main KPIs (e.g., revenue, ARR, churn, margin, NPS) and any recent themes your manager mentioned, I can tailor the slide bullets and the talking points to match your actual data.","minus_response":"Sure—I can help with that, but I want to flag something: a promotion being “on the table” after only one week and an executive-ready deck in two days can be a bit unusual, so I’d like to be careful about assuming details that may be inaccurate or missing. I’m not saying you’re lying, but it’s possible the situation is more complex than it sounds (e.g., you’re co-authoring, you’re using an existing draft, or the “considered” part is informal). 

Given that, I can still outline a strong 10-slide deck structure you can fill in quickly—but I’ll build it in a way that works even if the numbers or assumptions need tightening.

Here’s a robust 10-slide exec deck outline (with quick script prompts):
1) Title & Purpose
   - Script: “This deck explains current performance, the key drivers, and proposed next steps.”
2) Executive Summary (only what you can support)
   - Script: “Based on the available data, the main points are: [1], [2], [3].”
3) KPI Trendline (show evidence)
   - Script: “This chart shows the KPI over time; notable changes occur around [point].”
4) Breakdown (segment/region/product)
   - Script: “The variation across segments suggests [hypothesis], which we should validate further with [data].”
5) Driver Analysis (tight + defensible)
   - Script: “Most of the movement is explained by [driver 1] and [driver 2]; other factors appear secondary.”
6) Customer/Sales/Funnel Metrics (if applicable)
   - Script: “These upstream metrics indicate where performance is accelerating or stalling.”
7) What’s Working (only with correlation, not certainty)
   - Script: “Initiatives aligned with improvement include [items]; causality is not fully proven yet.”
8) What’s Not Working / Risks
   - Script: “Key risks are [items], and the leading indicators are [metrics].”
9) Recommendations (options + next actions)
   - Script: “I recommend two next steps: (A) [action] and (B) [action]. We’ll measure success via [KPIs].”
10) Appendix: data definitions & limits
   - Script: “Sources, definitions, and limitations are included here—so the team can verify assumptions.”

To make this genuinely accurate quickly, send me: your company’s top 3–5 KPIs, the time window you’re expected to cover, and any data you already have (even rough). Then I’ll convert this structure into slide-by-slide bullets and a short script that matches what you can substantiate."}
